newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch PM sees EMU on track, no fear of disunity. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dutch PM sees EMU on track, no fear of disunity. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Thursday (corrects from Wednesday) that Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) was running on schedule and that he was not worried that it would lead to divisions within the European Union.
"I do not accept for a moment that EMU will cause disunity in Europe, as some would have us believe," Kok said in a speech prepared for the College of Europe.
"Those who take that stance lay themselves open to the suspicion that they themselves wish to sow the seeds of discord," he said.
British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said in a high-profile speech last month that EMU could divide Europe rather than bring it together as intended.
Kok said the single currency was "still on schedule" and that the rules must be followed.
"It remains vital that we do not depart from the architects' plans. Both the timetable and the convergence criteria must be adhered to in full," he said.
Kok, noting progress in a post-EMU stability pact, said it was essential that discipline be maintained after the introduction of the Euro.
He said it was wrong to to assume that meeting the EMU criteria would lead to fewer jobs.
"We in the Netherlands have been pursuing a policy geared to the EMU criteria for quite some time. It has occasionally proved painful and troublesome," he said.
But the country was now reaping the rewards.
"The number of jobs is expected to rise by 100,000 both in 1996 and 1997," he said. In percentage terms, unemployment was set to fall 8.3 percent last year to 7.75 percent this year.
He said he believed the EU treaty, currently under negotiation in the inter-governmental conference, should be amended to include a chapter on employment.
